fullPassage:
Today, I'm looking for a tiny animal that's hiding in one of Europe's most beautiful capital cities, Vienna. Now it's home to nearly 2 million people, but 50% of the city is green space. What I'm looking for is probably one of Europe's most critically endangered mammals.
Now, I've come really early to a graveyard to try to see some hamsters because this is one of the best times of day to see them. At this time of the day, there's nobody around so they don't have to avoid people while looking for food. These little ones have been in the area for decades, but now live among the dead because development has robbed them of the green fields they used to inhabit.
Look! I just found one over there. See how it is trying to stuff its cheeks full? Hamsters can pack a quarter of their body weight inside their cheeks, which helps them get through the winter. Surprisingly, they not only feed on nuts and flowers, but have also adapted to eating candle wax, which is a good source of fat and is easy to find in graveyards.
Even though the hamsters here have adapted to the noises of the city, they still keep a watchful eye, as predators are never too far away. They may need to quickly escape back down into their holes, which are complex structures stretching under the ground. Despite urban areas generally having a negative effect on wildlife, cities can actually provide islands of protection for it.

questions.passage: Today, I'm looking for a (A)[tiny / huge] animal that's hiding in one of Europe's most beautiful capital cities, Vienna. Now it's home to nearly 2 million people, but 50% of the city is green space. What I'm looking for is probably one of Europe's most (B)[critically / slightly] endangered mammals. Now, I've come really early to a (C)[graveyard / playground] to try to see some hamsters. At this time of the day, there's nobody around so they don't have to avoid people while looking for food. These little ones have been in the area for decades, but now live among the dead because development has robbed them of the green fields they used to inhabit.
questions.stem: 다음 글의 (A), (B), (C)에 들어갈 말로 가장 적절한 것끼리 짝지은 것은?

det.korean: 작은(tiny) 동물을 찾고 있으며, 유럽에서 가장 심각하게(critically) 멸종 위기에 처한 포유류이고, 묘지(graveyard)에서 햄스터를 보려고 왔다.
det.analysis:
✅ ① tiny — critically — graveyard: 원문 일치
❌ ② huge(거대한): 원문은 tiny(작은)
❌ ③ slightly(약간): 원문은 critically(심각하게)
❌ ④ playground(놀이터): 원문은 graveyard(묘지)
det.tip: tiny(아주 작은) ↔ huge(거대한), critically(심각하게/치명적으로), graveyard(묘지) = cemetery

questions.passage: At this time of the day, there's nobody around so they don't have to avoid people while looking for food. questions.stem: 다음 글의 (A), (B), (C)에 들어갈 말로 가장 적절한 것끼리 짝지은 것은?

det.korean: 이 작은 동물들은 수십 년간(decades) 이 지역에 있었지만, 개발이 그들의 녹지를 빼앗았고(robbed), 볼을 음식으로 채우려(stuff) 하고 있다.
det.analysis:
✅ ② decades — robbed — stuff: 원문 일치
❌ ① granted(부여하다): robbed(빼앗다)의 반의어
❌ ③ moments(순간들): decades(수십 년)과 반대. 오랜 기간 거주
❌ ④ empty(비우다): stuff(채우다)의 반의어
det.tip: decades(수십 년), rob A of B(A에게서 B를 빼앗다), stuff(채우다/쑤셔넣다) ↔ empty(비우다)

det.korean: 촛농을 먹는 것에 적응했고(adapted), 도시의 소음(noises)에도 적응했으며, 여전히 경계하는(watchful) 눈을 유지한다.
det.analysis:
✅ ③ adapted — noises — watchful: 원문 일치
❌ ① silence(고요함): 도시 환경이므로 noises(소음)가 적절
❌ ② refused(거부하다): 적응했다는 맥락이므로 adapted(적응하다)가 적절

questions.stem: 다음 글의 밑줄 친 단어 중 문맥상 부적절한 것은?

det.korean: 유럽에서 가장 심각하게 멸종 위기에 처한(endangered) 포유류이다. abundant(풍부한)는 endangered(멸종 위기)의 반의어.

❌ ① hiding: 원문 일치. 숨어 있는 작은 동물
❌ ③ best: 원문 일치. 가장 좋은 시간
❌ ④ avoid: 원문 일치. 사람들을 피하다

questions.stem: 다음 단어의 반의어를 고르시오. endangered

det.korean: endangered(멸종 위기에 처한)의 반의어는 thriving(번성하는)이다.
det.analysis:

❌ ④ extinct(멸종된): endangered의 더 심한 단계
